title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
layout_note: Top row: the LLM context window as a horizontal strip of coloured blocks (System Instructions, Working Context, FIFO Queue in a dashed 'Prompt Tokens' frame, then Output Buffer in a dashed 'Completion Tokens' frame) under a curly brace labelled with the window size. Bottom row: the memory managers and external stores (Archival Storage cylinder, Function Executor, Queue Manager, Recall Storage cylinder) with thick arrows up into the top row.
grouping: The context window is grouped by a top curly brace and two dashed rectangles (prompt vs completion tokens); each memory region is identified by its fill colour (black system instructions, orange working context, magenta+blue FIFO queue, green archival storage, blue recall storage), and the arrows into each region take that region's colour.
shapes_depth: Flat solid rectangles for context segments with bold white or black serif labels; light-grey rounded rectangles for the two managers; the two storage tiers are 2.5-D cylinders (database drums); arrows are thick block arrows coloured by the memory they write to.
proposed_highlight: Each memory tier is named in bold and colour-coded, and its access rule (Read-Only / Read-Write, 'Write via Functions' / 'Write via Queue Manager') is written in bold directly beneath it, so the OS-style memory hierarchy is the figure.
lesson: Draw a context window as a single strip of coloured segments under a brace, and let every arrow that writes into a segment take that segment's colour.
notes: venue = arXiv (no venue printed on the arXiv first page; not recalled with confidence); year = arXiv preprint year. The FIFO Queue block has a small magenta segment at its left end (the recursive summary) whose colour matches one of the up-arrows from the Queue Manager.

taxonomy.task: virtual context management for LLMs with tiered memory

core.what: the LLM's finite context window drawn as one strip of coloured segments under a brace on top, with two managers and two external storage cylinders in a row below that read and write into it through colour-matched block arrows

relations.form: a green Archival Storage cylinder at the bottom left exchanges two green block arrows with the Function Executor; a blue Recall Storage cylinder at the bottom right receives a blue arrow from the Queue Manager and returns a long blue U-shaped arrow under the row to the Function Executor

the context window is drawn as a strip of segments (black System Instructions, orange Working Context, a magenta head plus blue FIFO Queue) inside a dashed 'Prompt Tokens' frame, with a separate dashed 'Completion Tokens' frame holding the Output Buffer, each segment captioned with its read/write rule
a short arrow runs from the FIFO Queue right to the Output Buffer, the prompt-to-completion order of the window

short upward block arrows tie each manager to the exact segment it writes: orange from the Function Executor into Working Context, magenta and blue from the Queue Manager into the FIFO Queue head and body; a black double arrow joins the two managers

channels.colour: segment fill = memory region (black system, orange working context, magenta/blue queue, green archival, blue recall), and each block arrow takes the colour of the memory it touches - so blue means both the FIFO Queue and Recall Storage
channels.shape: flat bars = in-context memory; cylinders = external storage; grey rounded boxes = managers
channels.line: thick block arrows = read/write actions; thin arrow = token order to completion
channels.frame: dashed frames = prompt vs completion tokens; a brace = the whole finite context window

quality.strengths: the core idea - a bounded window paged against external stores - is geometry: the window is a single strip on top under a brace, the stores sit outside it below, and every write arrow lands on the exact segment it changes; each region is captioned with its read/write rule
quality.weaknesses: blue codes both the FIFO Queue and Recall Storage, so the queue-to-recall eviction and recall-to-executor retrieval are hard to tell apart; the recall-to-executor arrow is a long U-turn under the whole row; no actual tokens or messages are drawn, only labelled bars

insights.structure: Two horizontal rows: the LLM context window as a strip of four coloured segments under a brace on top, and the managers (Function Executor, Queue Manager) flanked by Archival and Recall storage cylinders on the bottom.
insights.data: Memory regions are solid colour bars sized roughly by role (System Instructions black, Working Context orange, FIFO Queue blue with a magenta head), external stores are database cylinders, and no actual tokens or text are shown.
insights.emphasis: Bold two-line captions under each region state its read/write rule, and colour-matched block arrows (orange, magenta, blue, green) tie each manager action to the exact memory it changes.
insights.flow: Arrows run mostly bottom-to-top from managers into the context strip, sideways between storages and managers, and a large U-shaped blue arrow returns from Recall Storage under the row back to the Function Executor.
insights.avoid: Black and blue double-headed arrows between the two managers and the long U-shaped return arrow carry no label, so the read path from recall storage has to be inferred from the captions.

arrangement.units: a top lane holding the context window as coloured segments in dashed prompt/completion frames under a brace, and a bottom lane holding two grey manager boxes between two storage cylinders
arrangement.inputs_as: no explicit input; the context segments are labelled bars
arrangement.shared: the Function Executor is the single hub connected to archival storage, working context and recall storage

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
